author: @luigifranceschi2350
text:
I’m the fleet manager for our company group. We have 50 vehicles. We are located in the alps and we need vehicles that perform well in steep and winding roads. We have decided to slowly pass to electric due to low maintenance, low fuel cost, and also because in the mountain roads the electric cars usually perform really well. They have a nice kick, that is useful to pass slow vehicles, and thanks to regen downhill the advantage on fuel costs becomes even greater than on the flat  compared to ICE, because all the potential energy of an ICE vehicle downhill gets dissipated in heat at the breaks or using the low gears to slow down. while in an EV is put back in the battery.
Or at least this is what Teslas do. We already have one in the fleet. So that is a fact for me.
Due to image issues I wasn’t planning to buy more teslas, and pass to BYD. So I tested 2 of them. Unfortunately the regen is too weak even at the strongest level. I was forced to use the breaks all the way down. And that is bad. Not only because I’m not recovering all the potential energy, but mostly because I risk of overheating the breaks. And that is really bad. So until they don’t come with a more powerful regen setup BYD is a no for us. I really don’t get why BYD doesn’t improve on that part. For the rest are beautiful cars. The interior are far better than teslas and and the cars seems overall more solid and there is a wider choice, so I could have accommodated all the different needs with just one brand, that means just one shop for the maintenance.

author: @TM3PnrbringRecord
text:
I've tested both these cars and I've got to say that many things were wrong in this video. First thing is that the BYD Sealion or any BYD, has no Youtube, Netflix or anything similar integrated into the infotainment system, especially when the screen looks so bad (on all models). You can however use Apple Carplay or Android Auto to mirror it, but the quality is just bad and it will be using your phone's data unlike the Teslas having their own data. On the Tesla, many people still use Netflix, Youtube and the rest while charging, it's not really a gimmick but a comfort. These cars having 14 speakers makes you enjoy films like you're in a cinema, especially late at night when it's darker.

The doors on the Tesla are quite straightforward and I would even say very nice to use. They blend in well with the car's shape and the interior door button is very satisfying to use, seems luxurious but, many new passengers still try to pull on the emergency lever thinking it's the main door lever.
The autonomy, speed, interior space, infotainment, charging prices, aftersales support, quality and how easy it is to drive, all goes to Tesla without a doubt. The things that they messed up like the stalks and the lack of buttons can be fixed with simple aftermarket mods that actually work amazingly well and are very responsive.
Also, driving the Sealion is horrible. It wobbles horribly on corners and it even bounces sometimes when accelerating from 0mph and is unstable. Reminds me much of the Mustang GT Performance, which I also disliked a lot, especially when I actually love Fords.

This video feels very biased against Tesla and could either be a silent sponsorship or politics.

My verdict as an actual car tester: Teslas are great cars, if not, the best on the current market.

author: @MeanMachine1992
text: As an electrical engineer, I laugh every time I hear someone claim a Chinese product is equal to or better than a something made in the US or Germany or France or Japan. If you go through the brands that are used far and wide across industries for simple electrical and electronic needs, you come up with names like Omron, Telemecanique, Siemens, Schneider, GE, Honeywell and so on. A step down would be Hyundai, LS and Delta. If you've ever worked with electrical equipment, servo/step motors or even simple traditional squirrel-cage motors, you'd know the difference between a pure Chinese product and one that comes from a reputable company, even one that has its production line in China. Everything from the ball bearings to the dimensions of the copper wire and in most cases even the copper in the wire itself vastly differ in quality. The end result is that when the damn thing is new, you can see a small difference between the two that can't justifying paying so much more for a reputable brand. But once a year or two passes, you start noticing just how subpar Chinese products really are.

author: @TheEletricboy
text:
Some useful tesla-related advice and recommendations from experience:

1. Mirrors - you can click the steering wheel roller to toggle between left/right mirror.
2. You can add a few quick selection buttons at the bottom of the screen (I like having the seats, steering wheel heating, windshield defog).
3. You can quickly change AC temperature by just swiping left/right with your finger and it you dont have to take your eyes off the road (I even put a "macro" on the left steering wheel scroller which when held for 1s let's me adjust temp by scrolling without taking my hands off the wheel).
4. Android Auto/apple car play - the tesla maps are just the google api so it's exactly the same, plus if you like searching for a favourite saved place on your maps app through your phone you can just click "share" on google maps and select the tesla app, it will send it to your car's screen.
5. Spotify and youtube music come as part of the tesla OS, I don't have the premium versions so I just used a cracked youtube music on my phone and play it through bluetooth, it starts playing as soon as I enter the car so it there's no let-downs from my use case.
6. Suspension - it's one of the most comfortable suspensions I've ever felt (I've only ever had renaults, VWs, older BMWs so it's as close to luxury as my poor ass has ever been).

This is not a hard concept, get it together please. ⁠​⁠​⁠​⁠​⁠​⁠​⁠​⁠@jacksmith-mu3ee 1) The fact that Tesla uses BYD batteries doesn’t mean anything. It doesn’t make the BYD better, and the Tesla is still faster and better to drive despite using BYD batteries.

7:48 3.4 3.5 bar tire pressure is a lot, the tire side wall will loose its flexibility and become hard like you're riding on concrete wheels, every pothole, every speed bump will feel like you crashed into a wall, and the road grip will suffer immensely, (ever heard of car racers air down to 1.9 bar in track use) put 2.2 bar  up to 2.5 max you will feel the difference, the steering will feel more connected, more nimble, and the suspension would certainly dampne better, i'm talkling about things i experience everyday, i sometimes air up for " hyper milling purposes" and somtimes i airdown for comfort, and road driving pleasure, i set it at 2.3 2.5... perfect. when hyper miling i put 3.7 bars, and omg the comfort is disgusting, and the steering is like touchy but the car doesn't grip, so you don't feel like you're pulling g forces (like actually moving the car left and right) like fr, the car feels not enjoyable at all to drive.

edit: and yeah what had to arrive arrived, i'm at 22:34 , and yea, that's what i said those clunks are the concrete tires you got instead of rubber, air it down and you'll feel the difference. yeah, tires are very important stuff, set your tire pressure before starting to drive (set when cold, so before driving, then the tires would warm up, and the pressure would go up)
